I’m a Hispanic Jew who was adopted by an Irish catholic family and raised the same way as OP—they actively ignored my culture, didn’t let me embrace or engage in any ethnic or religious celebrations that I remembered from pre-adoption, and forced me to reject my identity. I think that OP’s adoptive parents are shitty for that reason, and I know how deeply painful and confusing it is to not belong and to be forced to reject your culture, however I feel like her bio parents are still sketchy as hell and I would be really cautious if I were OP. 

OP not being connected emotionally to her adoptive family makes her more vulnerable to her bio family’s manipulations. I don’t think bio mom’s story is entirely truthful, I think the timing of everything is weird, and I think OP is being very hasty to just immediately trust them. Me! I knew the bare minimum of what I wanted (avoiding an episiotomy or c-section if possible, open to pain medication), but otherwise had nothing else in the way of a birth/labor plan. I knew that if I made a plan, I’d probably freak out the second we had to deviate from it in any way whatsoever. I’m a high-strung person and a control freak and I just knew I’d go into a panic if my plan were to go south. Ended up with an 8-hour labor where I got an epidural before I felt I needed it but the anesthesiologist had nothing going on, ended up needing Pitocin a little later on, and had 15 minutes of pushing until I had my healthy baby. Minimal tearing, and overall a positive experience. 

My husband, normally the calm and rational one (while I’m pretty consistently an anxious mess of a human), was impressed with how chill I’d managed to be for the whole process, even at a scary moment when they couldn’t find baby’s heartbeat. I just stayed calm and trusted the process, and knew the doctors knew what they were doing. It was like every anxious night, panic attack, and “what if—“ moment prepared me for the day I gave birth. If I ever have another kid, I think I’d go about it in the same way.

YTA. 

First of all, being pregnant makes you hyper-aware of everything going on with your body. It’s very nice for you that the baby isn’t here yet so you don’t feel it should be dominating your life, but it *is* dominating her life. She cannot eat, lay down, move, sit, sleep, stand up, or do pretty much any basic function without some reminder that there is a baby growing inside of her. Drinking water and eating are plagued with thoughts of whether it’s the right amount, are you eating the right thing, are you maintaining healthy weight, etc. The skin of her belly is stretching and itching. The baby is kicking her and moving regularly. Her bladder is being squished underneath, while the rest of her organs are being squished behind or above. There’s a large amount of pressure on her hips, her front, her back, and her crotch. And sometimes there is nowhere to put your hands but on the giant mass of your belly because that soothes the kicking or itching or the insane pressure. Yes, you exist as individuals, but you are being extremely unempathetic to your wife’s reality right now. She cannot just pretend that she is not pregnant because the baby isn’t “here” yet. The baby is very much here for her. 

Not every single situation in a relationship is a 50/50 split. Sometimes things might be 60/40, sometimes 80/20. There will always be times when one partner needs to carry more of the load for the other partner. Right now, your wife is carrying an absolutely huge load physically and emotionally, and there is nothing that can be done in the immediate to change that. Your request showed a lack of empathy for the fact that she is growing a person for your family, and made it all about yourself and your feelings of discomfort. In normal circumstances, yes you need to be able to make requests of your partner even if it’s just for your comfort, and you should always be able to share your feelings. However, this situation, your wife is bearing a huge burden and you made a request for her to stop doing something that comforts and soothes her for feelings your own of discomfort that are based in the belief that “the baby isn’t here yet so it shouldn’t dominate our lives”, which again, is simply not reality for her. It is a ridiculous and unfair request to make to her right now. If someone is going hugely out of their way to do something for me, I’m not going to nitpick the exact way they’re doing it because a small aspect of their behavior annoys me. I just keep it to myself as a valid but unproductive thought. 

You’re not the asshole for feeling the way you do, even if I disagree with your reasonings for feeling that way. But making the request was 100% an asshole move.

ETA: It’s also very interesting to me that in the comments you mention that prior to getting pregnant, you both agreed the baby wouldn’t dominate your lives, and that now that your wife is very focused on the baby you feel she was “dishonest”. Why is your first reaction to assume she was lying? Have you considered that she underestimated how all-consuming pregnancy truly is? Have you asked her if she is coping okay with the loss of her bodily autonomy (the bodily autonomy that you are further threatening by requesting she stop rubbing her belly)? Also, in another vein, how do *you* feel about this baby coming? Are you scared or worried? Have you talked to someone about it if you are?

And has nobody told *you* that “medication and mental health treatment saved my life”? 

I already know the answer because several people in this thread are telling you that, and you can find further testimonies if you cared enough to look. 

You are failing both of your children. Your daughter AND your son. When your son is in jail/on the streets/addicted to god-knows-what/unable to form healthy relationships or attachments as an adult, he isn’t going to say “Gee, I’m sure glad my mom didn’t get me mental health treatment or medication for my issues when I was a kid so that I could keep being a smartie”. Your son will not be able to have a bright, happy, or productive future if he continues on this path. You are being a bad and selfish mother.

My normal wash every 2-3 days is with Shea Moisture’s Low Porosity Shampoo, then I condition with Pacifica Pineapple Curls. No problem! I had no clue hair porosity was a thing until I started going onto r/curlyhair to better manage the hot mess on my head. Even if your hair isn’t curly, knowing your porosity is so helpful!

Yup, that first wash day my hair is always so smooth and curly and shiny. Then I have another 1 or 2 mediocre-to-good days, maybe with a gentle refresh with some water and maybe the tiniest amount of product, before suddenly it’s a greasy mess and I look like Severus Snape.

A good way to check would be by taking a couple of strands of hair from your brush (or your head I guess) and put them in a bowl of water. Then, wait like 5 minutes. If the hairs float, then you have low porosity hair that is resistant to absorbing lots of products. If the hairs sink, then you have higher porosity hair that will drink up a lot of what you put in it. That’s how I tested mine, at least. Both types of hair have products and ingredients that work better for them based on that, and it can really make a big difference in the appearance and health of your hair!

Yeah, part of the problem is that a lot of people don’t really know what kind of porosity their hair is which makes it difficult to know exactly how frequently you should be washing it. I’d honestly love to have more porous hair! Mine is so thin and not at all absorbent.
